facts.statement: Marambionectes was an extinct plesiosaur that lived in Antarctica during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Marambionectes (meaning "Marambio Island swimmer") is an extinct genus of weddellonectian elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous López de Bertodano Formation of Antarctica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Marambionectes was discovered in 2018 near Marambio Island in Antarctica.
facts.quote: The Marambionectes holotype specimen, IAA-Pv 752, was discovered in 2018 in sediments of the López de Bertodano Formation (unit 9) near on Marambio (Seymour) Island of James Ross Archipelago, Antarctica.

facts.statement: Marambionectes molinai was formally described as a new genus and species in 2024 by O'Gorman and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2024, O'Gorman and colleagues described Marambionectes molinai as a new genus and species of elasmosaurid plesiosaur based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The species name molinai honors Argentinian fossil preparator Omar J. Molina for his field work in Antarctica.
facts.quote: The specific name, molinai, honors the Argentinian fossil preparator Omar J. Molina and his Antarctic field work.

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes a partial skeleton with vertebrae, ribs, a jaw, some teeth, and limb bones.
facts.quote: The specimen is partially articulated and incomplete, consisting of the basioccipital, mandible, some teeth, cervical, pectoral, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae, ribs, an ilium, the right humerus and ulna, and a femur.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen represents an adult individual of the species.
facts.quote: The specimen belongs to an adult animal.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Marambionectes within the Weddellonectia clade as the sister group to the Aristonectinae.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, O'Gorman et al. (2024) recovered Marambionectes as a derived member of the elasmosaurid clade Weddellonectia, as the sister taxon to the Aristonectinae.

facts.statement: Marambionectes is classified as a reptile belonging to the family Elasmosauridae and the parent group Weddellonectia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Weddellonectia Family: Elasmosauridae Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Marambionectes lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The scientific description of Marambionectes sparked controversy because the researchers used AI-generated images to illustrate the animal.
facts.quote: The description of Marambionectes created controversy within the paleoart community when the researchers used AI-generated images to depict the species.
